subject: science
notes: Skeletal muscles contain two main types of fibers, often called slow-twitch and fast-twitch.
Slow-twitch fibers contract relatively slowly, but because they rely heavily on oxygen to produce energy, they can keep working for long periods without tiring.
Fast-twitch fibers contract quickly and powerfully but tire much sooner.
The proportion of each fiber type varies from person to person and from muscle to muscle.
Elite marathon runners tend to have a high proportion of slow-twitch fibers in their leg muscles, whereas elite sprinters tend to have more fast-twitch fibers.
stem: The student wants to emphasize a difference in how quickly the two types of fibers tire. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Elite marathon runners tend to have more slow-twitch fibers in their legs, whereas elite sprinters tend to have more fast-twitch fibers.
choices.B: Fast-twitch fibers contract quickly and powerfully, while slow-twitch fibers contract relatively slowly.
choices.C: Slow-twitch fibers can work for long periods without tiring, but fast-twitch fibers, though powerful, tire much sooner.
choices.D: The proportion of slow-twitch and fast-twitch fibers varies both from person to person and from muscle to muscle.

explanation.why: The notes describe several differences between the fiber types, but the goal names one: how quickly they tire. Slow-twitch fibers can work a long time without tiring; fast-twitch fibers tire much sooner.
explanation.A: Incorrect. This is a difference, but between two kinds of athletes, not in how quickly the fibers tire.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is a real difference between the fibers, but it concerns how fast they contract, not how fast they tire. It is the most tempting near miss.
explanation.C: Correct. It contrasts slow-twitch fibers, which work for long periods without tiring, with fast-twitch fibers, which tire much sooner.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This describes variation in how common each type is, not how quickly either type tires.
